verdict.rationale: Decagon's Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs) are a first-party feature for encoding SOP-style agent behavior in natural language, and non-technical teams can author and iterate on them. That covers the core 'encode SOPs' part of the story. The evidence never says AOPs run step-by-step or branch deterministically, and natural-language definition suggests the model interprets them rather than executing fixed paths. Missing for 10: evidence of step-by-step execution, deterministic branching logic, per-issue-type routing to specific procedures, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, I encode standard operating procedures the agent follows step-by-step for known issue types, with deterministic branching

citations.quote: you can define agent behavior in natural language, the same way you train human agents with SOPs
